statement: To change the name on your Social Security record, file Form SS-5 (Application for a Social Security Card) and show original documents proving your legal name change, such as a court order, and proof of identity.
detail: You can file by mail or at a local Social Security office. There is no fee. Updating Social Security early helps other agencies that check your record.

cost.note: Social Security does not charge a fee for a corrected card.

timeline.typical: 2–4 weeks for the updated card to arrive

source.title: SSA Form SS-5, Application for a Social Security Card

statement: Federal policy on the sex/gender marker held in Social Security records has changed recently and is being litigated.
detail: Because this is volatile, the navigator does not present a current rule here; it must be reverified against the official source before being shown as fact.

statement: To update the name on your U.S. passport, submit a passport application with a certified copy of the document that legally changed your name, such as a court order.
detail: If your most recent passport was issued within the last year, the correction may be free; otherwise you apply with Form DS-82 (renewal by mail) or DS-11 (in person) and pay the applicable fee.

cost.note: Free for recent passports corrected within a year; otherwise standard application fees apply.

timeline.typical: several weeks; expedited service is available for an extra fee

source.title: U.S. Department of State — Change or Correct a Passport

statement: Federal policy on the sex marker printed in U.S. passports has changed recently and is subject to ongoing litigation.
